correctness.rationale: For all finite simple H on k≥3, comparison equality of Gaussian-exposed zonotope vertices reduces to identical edge orientations, giving an exact 2k-dimensional conditional-leaf integral. Only corner pairs (0,0),(1,1) contribute on n^-2 scaling; a uniform exponential majorant validates dominated convergence. Independent exponential rankings within each corner-color class yield q(H[S])q(H[V\S]), proving the coefficient and the collision-conditioned core-color distribution. An adjacent-pair swap proves strict q-monotonicity under edge addition, and Vandermonde gives sharp clique/edgeless bounds. Independently enumerated exact rational tests verify graph constants/monotonicity for all core graphs with at most four vertices and four small full graphs, while the proof establishes all k and n limits.

originality.rationale: The novelty claim is restricted to fixed arbitrary simple core graphs with at least three vertices, equal pendant leaves, the full k-dependent sharp collision coefficient, conditional two-color core law and strict edge-monotonic extremizers. The relevant full primary and published special-case texts were inspected; their orientation/linear-extension framework implies the finite integral setup but does not supply the high-leaf corner scaling and sharp graph partition functional. The k=1 and k=2 specializations are expressly credited and excluded. Unindexed equivalent general formulations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent result may exist in random graph-order comparison/linear-extension literature, despite the primary and direct special-case inspections.
The theorem fixes the core while the leaf count grows, so there is no uniform conclusion when the core grows with n.

value.rationale: The graph-dependent sharp leading collision coefficient and conditional localization classify the Euclidean angular statistics of a natural arbitrary-core leaf-blowup family. Adding one core edge strictly changes this physically interpretable invariant despite exponential numbers of underlying vertices; the sharp clique/independent-set extrema distinguish whole graph families. The result goes beyond existing one-hub and two-hub special cases and is a self-contained structural theorem rather than an unmotivated numeric table.
